question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren active, what must a driver do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Slow down and stay in lane.,c:Pull to the right and turn on four-way flashers.,d:Drive to the left shoulder and stop
note: You must promptly pull to the right and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely.

question: Which statement best describes drivers who have consumed alcohol and then drive?
options: a:They do not have sufficient control over their bodies, minds, or vehicles,b:They are always aware of the risks, c:They become better drivers because they are more careful
note: Alcohol is a depressant that reduces judgment, vision, coordination, and reaction time, impairing a driver’s ability to operate a vehicle safely.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?
options: a:Look and listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before a train appears.,c:Drive around lowered gates if a car is stuck on the tracks.,d:Keep radio volume high to hear signals better.
note: Always look, listen, and be ready to stop at tracks; do not go around gates or take risks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must a driver respond to a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and continue without stopping.,c:Merge to the right.
note: A flashing red light means stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If you socialize and drink alcohol, what is a safe option to ensure safe travel?
options: a:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.,d:Wait 10 minutes and then drive
note: Arranging a sober ride home prevents impaired driving; coffee or a shower does not reduce blood alcohol content.

question: Does talking or texting on a cell phone significantly increase crash risk?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Using a handheld or hands-free phone for talking or texting distracts you and increases the likelihood of a crash; it reduces attention and reaction time.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?
options: a:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles,b:The decreased stopping distance of trucks,c:The reduced noise levels from larger vehicles
note: Large vehicles need more distance to stop; smaller vehicles should avoid lingering in truck blind spots and give them extra space.

question: Which behavior describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Daydreaming or staring at objects off the roadway while driving.,b:Checking mirrors frequently and scanning traffic.,c:Watching only the car directly ahead.,d:Using turn signals when changing lanes.
note: Inattentive drivers are distracted by non-driving activities and do not adequately scan the road.

question: When making an emergency roadside stop, is it unnecessary to set the parking brake?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When you make an emergency stop, set your parking brake and turn on your emergency flashers to alert other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal situation requires you to come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when clear?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A steady yellow light
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: stop, yield to others, and proceed when safe.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams, where should you glance?
options: a:Toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Directly at the source of the light.,c:Toward the left side of the road.,d:At the center line for reference.
note: Glance to the right side of the road to avoid temporary blindness from glare while maintaining roadway position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit in business, residential, and school districts unless otherwise posted?
options: a:25 mph,b:15 mph,c:30 mph
note: Unless signs indicate otherwise, the speed limit for passenger vehicles and motorcycles in business, residential, or school areas is 25 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left at an intersection, what is important to do?
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians,b:Sound your horn to warn oncoming traffic,c:Swing to the right side of your lane to make room
note: Before making a left turn you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians; do not turn unless the way is clear and it is legal to do so.

question: What type of signs are typically orange?
options: a:Work zone and construction signs.,b:Regulatory signs like speed limits.,c:School zone signs.,d:Recreational area signs.
note: Orange signs warn of work zones or construction and alert drivers to changing conditions ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' sign mean?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.,b:The reduced speed begins at the next sign.,c:You have plenty of time to slow down before the zone.,d:The advisory speed begins after the sign
note: A posted reduced speed sign indicates the new posted speed limit begins at that sign.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should drivers do?
options: a:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always stop even if no children are present.,c:Always sound your horn when children are near.,d:Drive at normal speed if no crossing guard is present
note: Always yield to pedestrians and be alert for children who may enter the crosswalk or roadway unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb required?
options: a:Yes — it is required by law and a good habit,b:Only if other traffic is present,c:Only during the maneuver itself, not beforehand
note: You must signal your intentions in advance (Virginia requires signaling at least 100 feet before changing lanes or turning) so other road users can anticipate your actions.

question: What should you adjust first when you sit in a vehicle before driving?
options: a:Your seat.,b:Your rearview mirror.,c:Your seat belt.
note: Adjust your seat first so you can reach the controls and see the road, then set mirrors and fasten your seat belt.

question: Signs that warn drivers about hazardous conditions are called what?
options: a:Warning signs,b:Regulatory signs,c:Information signs
note: Warning signs (usually yellow with black symbols) advise drivers of potentially hazardous conditions ahead and should be obeyed for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is correct?
options: a:Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding is safe if you are skilled.,c:Speed has no effect on crash severity.,d:Speeding never results in fatalities
note: Both driving too fast and driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous; speed increases crash severity and risk.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:When changing lanes,b:When turning left or right,c:When pulling toward or away from a curb,d:All of the above
note: Check blind spots any time you intend to change the vehicle's position—turning, changing lanes, or parking.

question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much lateral space as possible.,b:Honk to warn them you're passing closely.,c:Drive in the bike lane to get around them.,d:Pass very quickly with no additional clearance.
note: Give bicyclists ample space when passing; do not crowd them and avoid passing too quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals stop working, how should you indicate a turn?
options: a:Use hand signals,b:Use your horn,c:Flash your headlights,d:Use your hazard lights
note: If turn signals fail, use standard hand signals to indicate turns or lane changes.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Traffic signal is malfunctioning and should be ignored.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow and proceed carefully through the intersection.

question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:
options: a:Signal, slow gradually, check rearview and watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Speed up and turn sharply.,c:Turn from any lane available without signaling.,d:Rely solely on the horn to warn others.
note: Signal in advance, reduce speed progressively, and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: Which is NOT a main factor in determining how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Perception and reaction distances.,c:Braking distance.,d:Vehicle speed and road conditions.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance — steering skill is not a primary factor.

question: What helps a person overcome the influence of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Only the passage of time,b:Hot coffee,c:Fresh air,d:Tomato juice and lime
note: Nothing speeds sobering except time—coffee, fresh air, and other remedies do not eliminate alcohol impairment.

question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Traffic in the indicated lane must turn in the direction shown and has a protected movement.,b:It only applies on one-way streets.,c:You may go only if a circular green is also lit.,d:You must yield to pedestrians before turning
note: A green arrow gives the same general authority as a circular green but requires traffic in the indicated lane to turn in the arrow's direction, usually with protected right-of-way.

question: What can occur if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine,b:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol,c:The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold
note: Alcohol and many medications interact, often increasing impairment and the risk of dangerous side effects; combining them can multiply their effects.

question: How does distraction typically affect a driver's reaction to hazards?
options: a:Makes drivers react more slowly,b:Makes drivers react more quickly,c:Has no effect,d:Improves lane-keeping
note: Distracted drivers react more slowly and are more likely to miss hazards, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass on the right of another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is waiting to turn left and there is a safe available lane to pass,b:Even if it requires driving off the pavement,c:On a narrow bridge,d:Only when signposted
note: You may pass on the right if the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a safe, available lane; you may not leave the paved roadway to pass.

question: Do pedestrians always have the right-of-way in crosswalks and intersections?
options: a:Yes when they are crossing at intersections—TRUE,b:No—FALSE,c:Only in marked crosswalks,d:Only when traffic lights say so
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing at intersections; crosswalks exist at intersections whether marked or not.

question: Which is true about vehicle tires on a wet roadway?
options: a:Higher speeds reduce tire effectiveness and can cause hydroplaning,b:Cars with good tires are unaffected by water,c:Deep water is safer than shallow water,d:Worn tires improve grip on water
note: As speed increases on wet roads, tires lose contact and may hydroplane. Slow down and avoid sudden maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red traffic signal light means you must:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection,b:Stop at the stop line,c:Stop before entering any crosswalk
note: A red signal requires stopping before entering the intersection, at any stop line, and before entering a crosswalk; do not proceed until the light turns green and it is safe.

question: What is the most common color used for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Green.,c:Red.
note: Most warning signs are yellow with black markings and are diamond-shaped to alert drivers of unexpected conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Check your rearview and side mirrors and look over your shoulder to check the blind spot,b:Turn on your headlights,c:Sound your horn to warn other drivers
note: Prior to changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to ensure your blind spot is clear before making the lane change.

question: Which substances can impair driving and lead to DUII?
options: a:Alcohol, controlled substances (illegal or prescription), and inhalants.,b:Only beer and wine.,c:Only illegal drugs, not prescriptions.,d:Only inhalants
note: A wide range of intoxicants — alcoholic beverages, illegal drugs, many prescriptions, and inhalants — can impair driving and result in DUII charges.

question: Why must you exercise increased caution when driving at night?
options: a:Drivers cannot see as well at night,b:Traffic volume is always greater at night,c:Vehicles move faster at night
note: Because of reduced visibility at night, you must use headlights between half an hour after sunset and half an hour before sunrise and otherwise drive more cautiously.

question: If your wheels slip off the pavement edge while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, then steer back onto the road when safe.,b:Jerk the wheel to force the vehicle back immediately.,c:Slam on the brakes and stop immediately.,d:Accelerate to get back on quickly
note: Keep control, slow gently, and steer back onto pavement when you have reduced speed; avoid sharp steering or braking.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood it tends to:
options: a:Slow your reactions and increase errors while driving.,b:Improve your coordination.,c:Make you less confident about driving.,d:Speed up your thinking processes.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, impairs judgment, and increases the likelihood of mistakes.

question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
options: a:Listen, look both ways, and proceed only when it is safe.,b:Cross quickly whenever you see a train.,c:Look both ways only when lights are flashing.
note: Before crossing tracks, look and listen for trains from both directions and only proceed when it is safe and clear.

question: Who receives vertical-format driver licenses in Virginia?
options: a:Persons under age 21.,b:Persons over age 21.,c:All drivers regardless of age.,d:Only commercial drivers
note: In Virginia, driver licenses and ID cards issued to persons under 21 are printed in a vertical format.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and safely turn around.,b:Back up on the shoulder to reach the missed exit.,c:Make a U-turn in the travel lane immediately.,d:Stop and wait for traffic to clear before turning around.
note: Do not back up or make dangerous maneuvers; go on to the next safe exit to turn around.

question: What effect does drinking coffee have on blood alcohol concentration after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.,b:Cancels the effect of the alcohol.,c:Decreases blood alcohol concentration.
note: Coffee does not reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC); it may make you more alert but does not sober you up.

question: What does an 'End school zone' sign indicate?
options: a:The end of a reduced speed school zone.,b:The start of a 20 mph zone.,c:That pedestrians are present more often.,d:A school crossing ahead
note: An 'End school zone' sign tells drivers that the reduced school zone speed limit has ended.

question: Which combination provides the most effective protection in a crash?
options: a:Both lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,b:Airbag alone.,c:Lap belt alone.,d:No restraint is necessary at low speeds.
note: Safety belts and airbags together offer the best protection, with belts being essential.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect driving?
options: a:It is a distracting activity.,b:It helps maintain alertness.,c:It does not affect driving ability.,d:It improves reaction time
note: Smoking can distract you by requiring you to take hands off the wheel or eyes off the road, increasing crash risk.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:To keep the front wheels straight.,c:In the opposite direction of the skid.
note: If your car skids, steer in the direction you want the vehicle to travel until it regains traction, then correct.

question: Which conviction can result in revocation or suspension of your driver license?
options: a:Operating a vehicle under the influence of alcohol or drugs.,b:Driving with snow on your car.,c:Failing to stop for a stop sign once.,d:Parking in a handicap spot without a placard
note: The DMV may suspend or revoke driving privileges for offenses including DUI, false statements to the DMV, or felonies involving a motor vehicle.

question: If involved in an accident, which action should a driver take immediately?
options: a:Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.,b:Always stand in the traffic lanes.,c:Leave the scene if no one appears hurt.
note: If in an accident you must stop at or near the scene, move your vehicle if possible to avoid blocking traffic, and avoid standing in traffic lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When doing so would interfere with traffic.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When the car in front of you is disabled.
note: You may cross broken lines to pass or change lanes only when it can be done safely and without interfering with traffic.

question: Are most work zone signs orange?
options: a:True — work zone signs are typically orange.,b:False — they are usually green.,c:Only temporary signs are orange.,d:They are always brown.
note: Work zone signs are generally orange and diamond-shaped or rectangular to warn drivers of work ahead.

question: Where are roads most likely to freeze quickly in cold or wet weather?
options: a:In shaded areas under trees or buildings.,b:On flat open stretches.,c:In the sun.,d:On bridges only
note: Shaded sections freeze earlier and dry last; exercise caution in shaded areas during cold or wet weather.

question: On long trips, what helps prevent drowsiness?
options: a:Stopping at regular intervals to rest,b:Turning on the radio loud,c:Driving faster than traffic,d:Opening windows only
note: Make scheduled stops for rest and stretching to avoid drowsiness on long trips.

question: What should a small vehicle driver anticipate when passing a large truck?
options: a:Wind gusts that can affect vehicle stability.,b:Loud music coming from the truck.,c:The truck will always slow down to let you pass.,d:No change in driving behavior is needed.
note: Large vehicles can create strong air turbulence that may push smaller vehicles; be prepared to correct steering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the correct lane, you should:
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,b:Turn from your current lane after signaling.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.
note: Do not make last-minute turns; proceed to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.

question: If a driver behind you is driving aggressively, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way,b:Stare at the driver as they pass,c:Speed up as they approach
note: If confronted by an aggressive driver, safely get out of their way, avoid eye contact, and do not engage or escalate the situation.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Drivers may not pass.,d:You must always stop before crossing it
note: A single dashed yellow line separates opposing traffic and permits passing when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a flashing red signal, what must you do?
options: a:Stop fully, then proceed when the way is clear.,b:Slow down and drive carefully through without stopping.,c:Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then go when safe.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be dangerous, what must you do?
options: a:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Cross the tracks quickly before the train arrives.,d:Flash your lights to warn the train
note: If a train is near or fast enough to pose a danger, you must wait until it has fully passed before crossing, even if warnings are absent.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:You may drive through the intersection if it is clear,b:You must slow down and prepare to stop,c:You must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding
note: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection when the way is clear; when turning you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstance may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To turn into or out of a driveway or make a permitted left turn.,b:To pass a slow-moving car anytime.,c:To pass another car on a hill.,d:Never under any circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing, but you may cross them to turn into driveways or make permitted left turns.

question: Are cell phones a serious source of driver distraction?
options: a:True — they are a serious distraction.,b:False — they do not affect driving.,c:Only for inexperienced drivers.,d:Only when used for texting.
note: Cell phones and similar devices can severely distract drivers; use only to report emergencies.

question: Compared with daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:More dangerous.,b:Less dangerous.,c:No more or less dangerous.,d:Always safer
note: Night driving is more hazardous due to reduced visibility, glare from headlights, and more drivers who may be tired or impaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:It has the same meaning as a circular red light — do not proceed,b:It means you may turn in the arrow's direction,c:It is never used as a traffic signal
note: A solid red arrow requires drivers to stop and prohibits movement in the direction of the arrow until it changes to green.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Always, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.,d:Only on weekends
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway regardless of how the pedestrian behaves; be prepared to stop for them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must drivers entering an interstate from an entrance ramp do?
options: a:Yield to traffic already on the highway.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Force their way into traffic.,d:Always drive at the posted ramp speed
note: Yield to vehicles on the interstate and merge safely when a sufficient gap is available.

question: What may happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both may be increased,b:Nothing will happen,c:The effects are canceled out,d:It makes you less impaired
note: Combining alcohol with drugs can magnify the impairing effects of each substance and increase danger.

question: What can drowsy drivers appear to be doing?
options: a:Driving in a manner similar to drunk drivers,b:Being extremely alert,c:Perfectly following the flow of traffic,d:Driving defensively
note: Drowsiness can impair driving to the point that a driver may appear intoxicated and respond poorly to hazards.

question: In what ways can alcohol affect you while driving?
options: a:It slows reaction time, impairs thinking, and can give false confidence.,b:It only affects drivers with little experience.,c:It always improves concentration.,d:It has no effect if you are well rested.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction, judgment, balance, and vision, and can create a false sense of confidence.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume?
options: a:Assume the driver may open the door as you approach,b:Speed up to get past quickly,c:Slam on your brakes
note: When passing parked cars, assume someone may open a door or step into traffic; leave extra space and proceed cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You have a green light and want to turn left but oncoming traffic is heavy. What should you do?
options: a:Use the next intersection to turn,b:Wait in the center of the intersection until the oncoming traffic clears,c:Stop at the crosswalk and wait for traffic to clear
note: When making a left turn, you may enter the intersection on a green light to wait for a safe gap, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before completing the turn.

question: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and carefully steer back onto the pavement.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Stop your car on the edge of the road.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, reduce speed without braking hard and carefully steer back onto the road when it is safe.

question: On slippery roads, what is the safest action to take?
options: a:Reduce your speed,b:Maintain the posted speed limit but be cautious,c:Speed up to get through the area faster,d:Increase following distance
note: When roads are slippery from rain, snow, or sleet, reduce your speed. You may need to drive slower than the posted limit for safety.

question: If someone drives much slower than the speed limit and blocks traffic, what should they do?
options: a:Pull off the road and let vehicles pass when traffic is backing up.,b:Always maintain their slow speed regardless of traffic.,c:Refuse to allow others to pass by speeding up.,d:Drive in the center of the lane to discourage passing
note: Driving significantly below the flow of traffic can be hazardous; if backing up traffic, move aside to let others pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What general rule should you follow regarding passing other vehicles?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed,b:Pass on the right whenever possible,c:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic at all costs
note: Passing increases crash risk; drive with the flow of traffic, obey speed limits, and only pass when necessary and safe.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop.,b:Slam on the brakes and stop immediately.,c:Speed up to reach a safe area quickly.,d:Steer sharply to the shoulder at once.
note: Do not brake hard; grip the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow gradually before pulling off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,b:Force their way into traffic.,c:Always have the right-of-way.
note: Yield to traffic on the public roadway and merge only when it is safe to do so.

question: A person carrying a white cane or using a guide dog is most likely:
options: a:A blind person.,b:A deaf person.,c:Part of a traffic study.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

question: How should you respond when approaching road construction or maintenance areas?
options: a:Be alert for flashing arrow panels, signs, and flaggers.,b:Drive in the middle of the lane and ignore speeds.,c:Pass other vehicles in the work zone.,d:Speed up to get through quickly
note: Drive near the middle of your lane, obey posted speeds, and heed flashing arrow panels, message boards, signs, and flaggers.

question: Does a double solid yellow line allow passing from either direction?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Double solid yellow lines mean vehicles in either direction are prohibited from crossing the centerline to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your left shoulder,b:Over your right shoulder,c:At your side mirror only
note: To check your blind spot, glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to ensure no vehicle occupies the space beside you.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light instruct drivers to do?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Merge only to the right.,c:Stop completely.,d:Yield to all traffic
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed with caution.

question: A court may suspend or revoke your driving privileges for which offense?
options: a:Reckless or aggressive driving (or other serious driving violations).,b:Always paying for gasoline.,c:Driving with a valid license.,d:Properly registering your vehicle.
note: Convictions for reckless/aggressive driving or other serious offenses can result in license suspension or revocation.

question: What defines your vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:Areas you cannot see without moving your head.,b:The area directly behind your vehicle.,c:What you see in your rearview mirror.,d:The area illuminated by headlights
note: Blind spots are zones beside and slightly behind your vehicle that cannot be seen in mirrors and require head movement to check.

question: When approaching a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog or cane, must you yield?
options: a:Yes—TRUE,b:No—FALSE,c:Only if they are in a crosswalk,d:Only at marked intersections
note: Pedestrians using assistive devices have the right-of-way and drivers must yield to them.

question: How do worn or bald tires affect driving?
options: a:They can increase stopping distance and make turning more difficult.,b:They improve fuel economy.,c:They have no effect on handling.,d:They decrease braking distance
note: Tires with low tread or bald surfaces increase stopping distance, reduce traction, and raise hydroplaning risk.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety step should you take?
options: a:Ensure you and all passengers have buckled safety belts.,b:Buckle only backseat passengers.,c:Buckle only child passengers.
note: Develop a routine: before starting the engine, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers are properly buckled.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic signal indicates that which light will appear next?
options: a:Steady red.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady green.,d:Flashing red
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal will soon change to steady red.

question: May vehicles without special disability plates or placards use designated disabled parking spaces?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Only vehicles displaying the appropriate Persons with Disabilities license plates, Disabled Veteran plates, or disabled parking placards may park in spaces reserved for persons with disabilities.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when entering a street from a driveway?
options: a:Stop before entering and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.,b:Honk to warn pedestrians.,c:Drive slowly and expect them to yield.,d:Enter as quickly as possible to avoid delaying traffic
note: Stop before crossing the sidewalk and roadway, yield to approaching vehicles and pedestrians, and only proceed when safe.

question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to which road users?
options: a:Vehicles already in the roundabout,b:Bicyclists and pedestrians within the roundabout,c:Both vehicles and pedestrians in the roundabout,d:Only emergency vehicles
note: Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and any vehicles already in the roundabout before entering.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space.,b:Turn wheels to the right immediately.,c:Turn wheels to the left before positioning.,d:Back straight into the space without aligning
note: After selecting a space and signaling, stop parallel to the car ahead of the space before turning your wheels to back into it.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:
options: a:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,b:Drive faster than the train to beat it across the tracks.,c:Look for a way around lowered gates.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign indicates you may need to slow or stop; obey signals and never go around lowered gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where are drivers prohibited from passing from either side?
options: a:Across a double solid yellow centerline.,b:Across a single broken yellow line.,c:Across a combination solid and broken centerline.,d:Where there is a dashed white line
note: A double solid yellow centerline means neither direction may cross to pass.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:Work zones may be stationary or moving and require extra caution.,b:They are always marked with black-and-white signs.,c:They do not require drivers to slow down.,d:They are only on highways.
note: Work zones can be fixed or moving and are marked with orange signs; drivers should slow down and pay attention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the best practice?
options: a:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to freeway speed and merge smoothly.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.,c:Turn on hazard lights until fully merged.,d:Merge at a much slower speed than traffic.
note: Blend into traffic by matching freeway speed on the acceleration lane; entering traffic must yield.

question: Is it safe to use cruise control when driving on snowy or icy roads if you drive at a reduced speed?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Do not use cruise control on snowy, icy, or slippery roads because it can cause loss of vehicle control if tires lose traction.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do regarding your vehicle lights?
options: a:Turn on your headlights (low beams),b:Drive using your parking lights,c:Use your four-way flashers instead of headlights
note: At dusk or on overcast days you must use headlights; use low beams within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles and 500 feet of a vehicle you are following.

question: Which factors commonly cause traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving, excessive speed for conditions, and following too closely,b:Vehicle paint color,c:Only bad weather,d:Streetlight outages
note: Inattentive driving, driving too fast for conditions, and tailgating are common causes of crashes.

question: If you are being tailgated and a right lane is available, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the right when safe, or if no right lane slow down gradually until the tailgater passes.,b:Brake sharply to teach the tailgater a lesson.,c:Speed up to create more space in front of you.,d:Ignore the tailgater and maintain exact speed.
note: If a right lane is open, move over; if not, slow down gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass—never brake abruptly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct sequence before changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot, then change lanes.,b:Signal and change lanes immediately.,c:Check mirrors only, then change lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check rearview and side mirrors, look over your shoulder to check the blind spot, and then move when safe.

question: When driving on slick surfaces, what should you do regarding the vehicle ahead?
options: a:Keep the usual following distance,b:Increase your following distance,c:Tailgate to reduce wind effects,d:Speed up to pass quickly
note: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead because it takes longer to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A green arrow pointing left.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A steady green circular light.,d:A flashing red light.
note: A steady green arrow gives protected right-of-way for the indicated turning movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving a private road or driveway onto a sidewalk, must you stop before crossing the sidewalk?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must stop before entering the street or crossing a sidewalk from a driveway, alley, building, or parking lot.

question: What does a diamond-shaped sign warn drivers about?
options: a:Existing or possible hazards ahead,b:School zone only,c:Public recreation areas only,d:Regulatory information
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of potential hazards or special conditions ahead and are usually yellow or orange.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic,b:Only in rural areas,c:When in heavy construction zones,d:When passing cyclists
note: Driving so slowly that you disrupt traffic flow can be illegal and may result in a citation.

question: For your own protection, which of these should you never do regarding your license?
options: a:Drive with a suspended or revoked license.,b:Carry your license in a wallet.,c:Keep your license clean and legible.,d:Always present it when requested by police.
note: Operating a vehicle with a suspended or revoked license is prohibited and endangers both you and others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians crossing a public street or highway.,b:Only cars in the same lane as you.,c:Only drivers turning left.,d:Only emergency vehicles with lights on
note: Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and to other entities entitled to right-of-way, including funeral processions and military convoys where applicable.

question: Which of the following best describes your responsibilities for the vehicle you drive?
options: a:Ensure it is properly registered, insured, and in safe working condition.,b:Only ensure it is insured.,c:Only ensure it is properly registered.,d:None of the above.
note: Drivers are responsible for registration, insurance compliance, and maintaining the vehicle in safe operating condition.

question: Can drivers park in the handicap parking access aisles beside accessible stalls?
options: a:No—FALSE,b:Yes—TRUE,c:Only with a permit,d:Only during certain hours
note: Parking in a handicap access aisle is prohibited; these spaces provide room for wheelchair access and lifts.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe
note: A double solid yellow line separates opposing traffic and prohibits passing or crossing the lines except to turn where permitted by law.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels run off the pavement, what is the safest action?
options: a:Take your foot off the accelerator, steer parallel to the road, slow, then ease back onto the pavement.,b:Immediately brake hard and stop.,c:Accelerate and swerve back onto the road quickly.,d:Turn sharply left to get back on the pavement immediately.
note: Do not oversteer; slow gradually and gently steer back onto the road when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal displays both a red light and a green arrow, is turning in the arrow's direction prohibited until the red light changes?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A green arrow allows drivers to turn in the arrow’s direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians in the intersection, even if a steady red or circular red light is also lit for other movements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you need to change lanes, what steps are important?
options: a:Signal ahead of the lane change, check blind spots, and make sure the lane is clear.,b:Change lanes immediately without signaling.,c:Sound your horn and move quickly.,d:Close your eyes briefly before moving
note: Always signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and only move when the lane is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main-traveled portion of the road,b:Demand the other vehicle pull over,c:Pull completely off and stop on the other lane,d:Speed up to pass first
note: On narrow roads, give oncoming traffic at least half of the main-traveled portion so both can pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the right yields to the left.,c:The faster vehicle proceeds first.,d:Both vehicles back up and wait.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign typically indicates what?
options: a:A road hazard or warning,b:An interstate route,c:A school crossing,d:A regulatory restriction
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards or special conditions ahead and are usually yellow (or orange in work zones).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm and hand extended downward is the hand signal for:
options: a:Preparing to stop.,b:Turning left.,c:Turning right.,d:Reversing the vehicle.
note: A left arm extended down indicates the driver intends to stop or slow down.

question: In bad weather, what should drivers do to following distance?
options: a:Increase their following distance,b:Decrease their following distance,c:Maintain the same following distance as in clear weather
note: Increase following distance in rain, snow, or other poor conditions to give yourself more time to react and stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it possible that 10 mph may be too fast in some conditions?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drive below posted limits when conditions (traffic, weather, visibility) require; sometimes very low speeds are needed for safety.

question: What color are signs that indicate public recreation areas and cultural sites?
options: a:Brown.,b:Green.,c:Red.,d:Orange.
note: Brown signs are used to identify cultural, historical, and recreational areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic,b:Other drivers already in the intersection only,c:No one — left turns always have the right-of-way
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection and yield to any traffic already in the intersection.

question: When backing a vehicle, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window; do not rely solely on mirrors.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Open the door to see behind you.,d:Back quickly to minimize time spent reversing
note: Before backing, check behind the vehicle and turn your head to look through the rear window; mirrors alone may not show children or small objects.

question: Is it legal to drive around or under railroad crossing gates or barriers?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Never drive through, around, or under lowered railroad crossing gates or barriers — doing so is illegal and extremely dangerous.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When you see a child about to run into the street.,b:When you are passing a bicyclist.,c:When you are traveling through an intersection.,d:When another driver is driving slowly
note: Use the horn as a warning when someone may not see you — for example, if a child suddenly runs into the road. Avoid using it for noncritical reasons.

question: Should motorists keep a safe following distance when near bicyclists?
options: a:Yes — always maintain a safe operating distance.,b:No — treat cyclists as pedestrians.,c:Only when passing on multi-lane roads.,d:Only in urban areas.
note: Drivers must be especially careful around cyclists and maintain a safe distance to allow room for maneuvering.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, what must you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop,b:Continue driving at same speed,c:Speed up and take the nearest exit,d:Stop in the middle of the street
note: On a one-way street, pull to the nearest curb or roadside and stop to yield to the emergency vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and lights approaches, the driver should pull to the right-hand edge of the roadway and wait for it to pass.
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must immediately pull to the right and stop to allow emergency vehicles using lights and sirens to pass.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted and driving with one hand while talking to a passenger, you should:
options: a:Give that vehicle extra space,b:Follow closely to observe them,c:Try to correct their driving,d:Flash your lights to warn them
note: Allow extra space because an inattentive driver reduces their safety margin and increases crash risk.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road ahead.,b:Directly into the oncoming headlights.,c:At the center line.,d:At the oncoming vehicle's windshield.
note: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded while still keeping enough view of the roadway.

question: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle you borrow, what should you do?
options: a:Familiarize yourself with the location and operation of controls and check for defects.,b:Start driving immediately because all vehicles are the same.,c:Ignore any odd noises to avoid embarrassing the owner.,d:Drive only at night to avoid others noticing.
note: Take time to learn where essential controls are and ensure any defects are corrected before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what signal are they giving?
options: a:They intend to stop.,b:They intend to turn right.,c:They intend to turn left.,d:They intend to slow then turn left
note: A left arm extended downward indicates the driver plans to stop or slow; adjust your driving accordingly.

question: If faced with an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, what should you do?
options: a:Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist when safe.,b:Split the difference and squeeze between both hazards.,c:Pass the bicyclist quickly regardless of the oncoming car.,d:Stop in the travel lane until both clear.
note: Avoid handling two hazards at once; let the car pass, then pass the bicyclist with ample space.

question: May you drive around lowered railroad gates to cross the tracks?
options: a:No—under no circumstances,b:Yes if the train has passed,c:Yes when lights stop flashing,d:Only if traffic is light
note: Never go around lowered gates at railroad crossings; wait until gates are raised and signals indicate it is safe.

question: At what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a driver age 21 or older legally intoxicated in Virginia?
options: a:0.08 percent,b:0.09 percent,c:0.07 percent
note: Drivers age 21 or older are considered driving under the influence if their BAC is 0.08 percent or higher; impairment and enforcement can occur at lower BACs depending on driving ability.

question: What most affects your ability to stop a vehicle safely?
options: a:Road and surface conditions (e.g., wet, icy, gravel).,b:The color of the vehicle.,c:The type of radio you are listening to.,d:Your favorite driving playlist.
note: Stopping distance is greatly affected by road surface and condition; reduce speed when roads are poor.

question: What purpose do highway pavement markings serve?
options: a:Provide information and guidance to drivers,b:Are only used in construction zones,c:Are mainly decorative,d:Warn only bicyclists
note: Pavement markings guide lane position, indicate passing zones, and warn drivers about conditions ahead.

question: Should drivers continually try to improve their driving and observation skills?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Because driving always involves risk, continuing to improve your driving and observation skills enhances safety.

question: Is it legal to transport children under 16 in the bed of a pickup truck with a camper shell?
options: a:No—FALSE,b:Yes—TRUE,c:Only with parental consent,d:Only on private property
note: Virginia law prohibits transporting children under 16 in the bed of a pickup truck even if it has a camper shell.

question: If you encounter an animal in the road, what should you do?
options: a:Pass slowly and cautiously to avoid startling it.,b:Honk loudly and swerve around it quickly.,c:Speed up to pass before it moves.,d:Attempt to chase it off the road.
note: Approach slowly and pass with care to prevent frightening the animal into unpredictable movement.

question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the roadway mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines mean no passing from either direction, except to turn left where permitted.

question: Is alcohol the leading factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:Yes—TRUE,b:No—FALSE,c:Only in certain states,d:Only among young drivers
note: Alcohol is a leading cause of fatal crashes because it impairs vision, judgment, and reaction time.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside large vehicles and do not tailgate,b:Always pass on the right,c:Flash your lights at them,d:Drive directly behind them closely
note: Large vehicles have extensive blind spots; avoid lingering beside them and do not tailgate to remain visible to the driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can a bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws be cited?
options: a:Yes—the bicyclist can be ticketed,b:No—bicyclists are exempt,c:They will always receive a warning,d:Only if riding in a bike lane
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motorists and can be cited for violations.

question: How should you wear your seat belt shoulder strap?
options: a:Across your shoulder and chest, not under your arm or behind your back,b:Behind your back for comfort,c:Under your arm to keep the lap belt lower
note: Wear shoulder and lap belts snugly: shoulder belt over the shoulder and across the chest; never put the shoulder belt under your arm or behind your back.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited due to safety concerns?
options: a:On hills and curves,b:At intersections,c:At railroad crossings,d:All of the above
note: Passing is unsafe and unlawful on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings.

question: When in a line of traffic crossing a railroad with no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have room to clear the tracks so you won't have to stop on them,b:You can pass slower drivers on the tracks,c:You always have the right-of-way,d:You may stop on the tracks if traffic backs up
note: Make sure your vehicle can fully clear the tracks before entering; never stop on the tracks or pass another vehicle there.

question: Which tests may the DMV require when you apply for a driver license?
options: a:Vision screening, knowledge test, and road skills test as applicable.,b:Only a knowledge test.,c:Only a road skills test.,d:No tests are required under any circumstances.
note: DMV may perform a vision screening and require knowledge and road skills tests depending on your application.

question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A flashing red light,c:A solid yellow light,d:A steady green light
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop if needed.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:Amount of food in the stomach, body weight, and time between drinks.,b:Only the number of drinks consumed.,c:Only the body weight of the person.,d:The color of the drink
note: BAC is affected by the amount of alcohol consumed, how much time passes between drinks, body weight, and whether you have eaten; food only slows absorption.

question: On a two-lane road, must drivers always stop for a stopped school bus with its lights flashing?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Drivers on a two-lane road must stop for a stopped school bus that is loading or unloading children, regardless of travel direction.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember trucks generally:
options: a:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.,b:Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.,c:Require a smaller turning radius than passenger cars.
note: Because of their size and weight, trucks need longer stopping distances than smaller vehicles and have larger blind spots.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal,b:Brake hard immediately,c:Maintain your current speed and keep straight
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas, and brake gently once you have control, then pull safely off the road.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Move it off the traveled portion of the roadway.,b:Always leave it where it stopped until police arrive.,c:Hide the vehicle and leave the scene.,d:Back up into traffic to clear the lane.
note: After a minor collision, move the vehicle out of traffic if it can be done safely; never leave the scene.

question: If your vehicle has airbags, what should you do to increase safety?
options: a:Wear seat belts and move your seat back at least 10 inches from the steering wheel,b:Disable the airbags,c:Sit as close to the steering wheel as possible,d:Lean forward while driving
note: Always buckle up, move the seat back at least 10 inches from the wheel, and tilt the wheel down if possible so airbag points to chest.

question: How should a lap belt be positioned for proper fit?
options: a:Buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen,b:Loose so it is comfortable,c:Hidden beneath the seat
note: Lap belts should be snug across the hip bones and low on the abdomen; shoulder belts should rest across the chest and shoulder, not under the arm or behind the back.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate?
options: a:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed for both directions.,c:Passing is allowed only uphill.,d:You may cross to pass whenever traffic is light.
note: Two solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate no passing for either direction.

question: Which kinds of drugs can impair driving ability?
options: a:Prescription and over-the-counter medications, illegal drugs, and some cold remedies,b:Only illegal drugs,c:Only prescription drugs,d:Only alcohol
note: Many drugs—including prescriptions, OTC medications, and illicit drugs—can impair driving; always check side effects before driving.

question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign typically:
options: a:Warns you about conditions on or near the road.,b:Directs you to nearby cities.,c:Gives regulatory rules like speed limits.,d:Indicates a rest area ahead.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

question: If you stop along the road at night, which lights should you use?
options: a:Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on,b:Turn off all lights,c:Use only parking lights,d:Use high beams
note: Activate emergency flashers and leave low beams on so other road users can clearly see your vehicle.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane adjacent to the broken line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,c:Passing is allowed in both directions.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, vehicles next to the broken line may pass; those next to the solid line may not.

question: What does Virginia's zero tolerance law for drivers under 21 mean?
options: a:It is illegal for those under 21 to drive with a BAC of 0.02% or higher.,b:Drivers under 21 are allowed up to 0.08% BAC.,c:It applies only to commercial drivers.,d:It means no alcohol-related laws apply to teens.
note: Drivers under 21 can be convicted of illegal consumption if their BAC is 0.02% or greater under zero tolerance laws.

question: What are Virginia's curfew hours for drivers under 18?
options: a:Midnight until 4 a.m.,b:8 p.m. until midnight,c:10 p.m. until 2 a.m.,d:9 p.m. until 1 a.m.
note: Drivers under 18 are generally prohibited from driving between midnight and 4 a.m., with certain exceptions.

question: Which in-vehicle activity increases crash risk the most?
options: a:Using a cell phone,b:Listening to the radio,c:Adjusting AC temperature,d:Looking in your rearview mirror briefly
note: Cell phone use, even hands-free, is a major distraction and increases crash risk significantly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When you are entering a street from a garage, driveway, or alley,b:When your signal is a green arrow,c:When another vehicle is on a road to your left and you arrive at an unmarked intersection at the same time
note: You must yield when entering a street from a garage, driveway, or alley and yield to pedestrians on intersecting sidewalks. A green arrow means you may proceed as directed after yielding to any traffic and pedestrians in the intersection.

question: Traffic lanes moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It gives you time to react to unexpected actions by other road users.,b:It prevents other drivers from changing lanes.,c:It keeps traffic flowing faster.,d:It reduces your fuel consumption.
note: A space cushion lets you respond safely to sudden events like braking or lane changes by others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If approaching a stop sign without a marked crosswalk, must you stop before entering the intersection?
options: a:True,b:False
note: At an unmarked stop, you must come to a complete stop at the point nearest the intersection where you can safely see cross traffic without entering the intersection.

question: How should you prepare for hazards on the road ahead?
options: a:Continually scan the entire roadway and roadsides.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Drive with your left foot resting on the brake.,d:Focus only on the vehicle directly ahead
note: Search the entire road and sides of the road to identify potential hazards early so you can respond safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns green, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to any pedestrians or vehicles legally in the intersection.,b:Accelerate as fast as possible.,c:Back up to recheck the intersection.,d:Honk to alert others you are moving.
note: A green light permits movement but you must first yield to pedestrians and traffic still in the intersection.

question: When are roads most slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:During the first 10 to 15 minutes.,b:After it has been raining for hours.,c:The day after it rains.,d:Only when temperatures are below freezing
note: Road surfaces can become slick in the first 10–15 minutes of rain as oil and residue rise to the surface, increasing skid risk.

question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic at a reasonable speed.,b:Drive much faster than other vehicles to pass quickly.,c:Drive much slower than the flow to be cautious.,d:Constantly change lanes to find gaps.
note: Traveling at a speed consistent with the flow of traffic (within limits) reduces the chance of collisions.

question: A flashing yellow arrow for left turns means you may:
options: a:Come to a complete stop before turning.,b:Turn left only when the intersection is empty.,c:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: Do ramps and bridges tend to freeze before roadways?
options: a:True — ramps and bridges can freeze sooner than roads.,b:False — they freeze at the same time.,c:Only rural roads freeze first.,d:They never freeze before roads.
note: Because bridges and ramps are exposed to air above and below the pavement, they can ice before regular roadway surfaces.

question: If you have a tire blowout while driving, which is the correct sequence of actions?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas, avoid heavy braking, slow gradually, then pull off.,b:Brake hard immediately and steer to the shoulder.,c:Speed up to reach a safe area quickly.,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply and stop in the travel lane.
note: Do not apply brakes suddenly; ease off the accelerator, slow gradually, and then pull safely off the road.

question: Which action can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time,b:Disobeying posted speed limits,c:Using improper turn signals
note: Allowing extra travel time, using turn signals properly, and obeying posted speed limits are ways to reduce stress and the likelihood of road rage incidents.

question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as which sign?
options: a:Yield sign.,b:Stop sign.,c:Solid red light.
note: A red flashing light means stop, just like a stop sign; come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.

question: May you drink alcohol inside a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:No — it is illegal to possess or consume alcoholic beverages on public roads.,b:Yes, if you are a passenger in the back seat.,c:Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.,d:Yes, as long as the driver is sober
note: Possessing or consuming alcohol on public roads is prohibited; open containers in areas occupied by driver or passengers are illegal.

question: Do you have to stop for a school bus on a private road when its red lights are flashing?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must stop for stopped school buses with flashing red lights and extended stop arms on both public and private roads unless local rules state otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians,b:Maintain a normal driving speed without stopping,c:Stop and check for nearby police cars first
note: You may turn right on a steady green unless a sign prohibits it, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on Virginia interstates in designated rural areas?
options: a:50 mph.,b:60 mph.,c:70 mph.
note: The maximum posted speed limit on certain rural interstate highways in Virginia is 70 mph unless otherwise signed.

question: Which practices improve night driving safety?
options: a:Increase following distance and ensure headlights work properly.,b:Drive faster to get through dark areas quickly.,c:Use parking lights instead of headlights.,d:Keep interior lights on brightly
note: At night, increase following distance, avoid driving when tired, and ensure headlights and other lighting are functioning.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is true?
options: a:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle,b:Motorcycles do not require the full lane width,c:It is okay to pass a motorcycle by mildly overlapping lanes,d:You may pass a motorcycle in a bike lane
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane; when passing a motorcycle, be sure you are entirely in the left lane before passing on the left.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, how should you safely pass a bicyclist traveling the same direction?
options: a:Slow down, wait until no oncoming traffic, then pass while leaving sufficient space,b:Continue straight — the bicyclist should get out of your way,c:Only pass at a traffic signal or stop sign
note: Pass bicyclists as you would any vehicle: ensure clear sight, allow adequate lateral space (at least 3 feet), and do not pass when unsafe.

question: If a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) starts to lose traction, what should you do?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer out of danger,b:Pump the brakes,c:Press and hold the gas pedal
note: For vehicles with ABS, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the system will automatically modulate braking to help you maintain steering control.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops and slow down gradually,b:Speed up to clear intersections,c:Brake abruptly to warn others,d:Turn off brake lights when stopping
note: Avoid sudden stops by easing off the accelerator and braking smoothly to give drivers behind time to react.

question: Which action should you take just before making a turn?
options: a:Activate your turn signal several seconds before turning.,b:Increase your speed to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Begin turning without signaling if traffic is light.,d:Brake abruptly just prior to turning.
note: Signal three to four seconds before turning to communicate your intentions to other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which pavement marking allows you to pass into the adjacent lane?
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Double solid yellow line.,c:Solid yellow line.,d:Double solid white line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed when safe to pass.

question: If you discover a defect that may affect safe operation of your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Have it corrected as soon as possible before driving.,b:Continue driving until it breaks down completely.,c:Ignore it if driving a short distance.,d:Only fix it when you get a warning light on the dash.
note: Any defect that could affect safe operation should be repaired promptly and before driving when possible.

question: At intersections with light rail, what must drivers always do?
options: a:Obey all traffic signals and look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Drive around lowered crossing gates.,c:Assume trains always yield to vehicles.,d:Ignore pedestrian presence near tracks.
note: Always obey signals, look both ways, and never drive around lowered gates; trains may share the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing other vehicles?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots, signal, then pass when safe.,b:Honk at the vehicle ahead before passing.,c:Re-enter the lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,d:Pass on the shoulder if traffic is slow
note: Ensure mirrors and blind spots are clear, signal, and only re-enter when you can see the passed vehicle’s front in your rearview mirror.

question: What is the safest way to transport small children in a vehicle?
options: a:Secure them in an appropriate child safety seat,b:Hold them in an adult's lap,c:Allow them to stand on the floor in the back
note: Children must be placed in properly sized and installed child safety seats or boosters; no adult can safely hold a child in a crash or sudden stop.

question: Which of the following can be penalties for a DUI conviction?
options: a:License suspension or revocation,b:Jail time,c:Fines and restitution,d:All of the above
note: DUI penalties can include license suspension/revocation, fines, jail, and other costs depending on the case.

question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams can reflect off the fog and reduce your visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal displays a steady green arrow for your lane, you may:
options: a:Turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Turn without checking for other vehicles or pedestrians.,c:Continue straight only.,d:Ignore other signs or lane markings.
note: A green arrow indicates a permitted turning movement, but you must still yield to those already in the intersection.

question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely solely on the left side mirror.,c:Look only at the rearview mirror.,d:Use your turn signal and assume it's clear
note: Quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to ensure the blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

question: Is nighttime the safest time for cyclists to ride?
options: a:Yes—TRUE,b:No—FALSE,c:Only in well-lit areas,d:Only when wearing reflective gear
note: Cyclists are harder to see at night even with lights or reflectors; extra caution is required for both cyclists and drivers.

question: What do pennant-shaped road signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:Speed limits.,c:School zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones; they are placed on the left side of the roadway to warn drivers.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.,b:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.,c:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, and pull to a safe area to stop.
note: If power steering fails, it will require more effort to steer; slow down and safely pull off the road as soon as possible.

question: If there are two parallel railroad tracks, what precaution should you take?
options: a:After one train passes, look for another train on the other track before crossing.,b:Assume the crossing is safe once one train passes.,c:Cross immediately as the first train clears.,d:Honk and drive around any remaining gates.
note: Multiple tracks can have trains traveling in either direction; always ensure all tracks are clear before crossing.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?
options: a:On the side of the road facing oncoming traffic.,b:On the same side of the road on which traffic is moving.,c:On the side of the road which has the lightest traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic so they can see approaching vehicles and drivers can see them.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb so a rolling vehicle will move away from traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn should you signal when preparing to turn?
options: a:About 100 feet (three to four seconds).,b:50 feet.,c:200 feet.,d:Immediately before turning
note: Signal about 100 feet or three to four seconds before your turn to notify other drivers of your intention.

question: Are drivers allowed to pass a school bus that is displaying flashing red lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights, all approaching traffic must stop and remain stopped until the lights are turned off, except vehicles on the opposite side of a divided highway with a median.

question: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of you, what is the proper response?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop, yielding the right-of-way.,b:Flash your lights to warn them.,c:Speed up and pass in front of them.,d:Sound your horn repeatedly
note: Always yield to pedestrians and be particularly cautious in areas where children are likely to appear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A “No stopping” sign means you may stop only to:
options: a:Avoid a conflict with other traffic,b:Unload packages at any time,c:Discharge passengers whenever you wish
note: A no stopping zone allows stops only to obey a traffic control device, obey a police officer, or to avoid a collision or conflict with other traffic.

question: When sharing the road with a motorcycle, what must you do?
options: a:Allow the motorcycle the full width of a travel lane.,b:Drive beside the motorcycle in the same lane.,c:Force the motorcycle to use half a lane.,d:Pass the motorcycle within the same lane.
note: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle and should be given a full lane to allow safe maneuvering.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,b:Reach down and try to pull the pedal up.,c:Shift to park immediately.,d:Turn off the radio and continue driving
note: Keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, brake steadily, pull off when safe, and turn off the engine.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following?
options: a:Driving too fast for conditions,b:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots,c:Yielding the right-of-way
note: A common cause of crashes is driving faster than conditions safely allow. Adjust speed for weather, visibility, traffic, and road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, what must you ensure before passing?
options: a:That the passing lane is clear.,b:You pass only on the right.,c:You honk before passing.,d:You exceed the speed limit while passing
note: Before passing you must verify the passing lane is clear and signal before changing lanes.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Even a small amount of alcohol can impair concentration, judgment, and memory.,b:Only very high BAC levels affect driving.,c:Alcohol improves nighttime vision.,d:Alcohol has no effect on driving skills.
note: Any alcohol can reduce perceptual and decision-making abilities and negatively affect driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do safely and legally?
options: a:Move into the oncoming traffic lane to complete the pass when it is safe,b:Flash your lights at oncoming traffic,c:Use the shoulder to pass
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road requires you to use the lane for oncoming traffic. Only pass when you have a clear view and it is legal and safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit in residential, school, or business zones unless posted otherwise?
options: a:25 mph.,b:15 mph.,c:30 mph.,d:35 mph.
note: Unless a different limit is posted, the speed limit in these zones is 25 mph for passenger vehicles and motorcycles.

question: At night, which is most difficult to see?
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Road signs.,c:Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are the hardest to see at night compared with signs or other roadside objects, so use extra caution.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In foggy conditions use your low-beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped). High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal displays a steady yellow arrow for a turn, what should drivers do?
options: a:Proceed with the turn after yielding,b:Slow to a stop if it is safe to do so,c:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that a red arrow is about to appear; you should stop unless you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely.

question: Which action most helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Reduce speed and increase following distance.,b:Engage four-wheel drive and maintain normal speed.,c:Get off highways immediately no matter the situation.,d:Drive with your hazard lights on constantly.
note: Slowing down and increasing following distance are the key techniques for safe winter driving.

question: When is it required to use your turn signal?
options: a:When changing lanes.,b:Only when turning at an intersection.,c:You do not need to signal when pulling into a parking space.
note: Always use the proper signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do first to warn them?
options: a:Sound your horn to alert the other driver.,b:Wave your arms out the window.,c:Turn off your headlights.,d:Flash your interior dome light.
note: Use the horn to warn others of imminent danger so they can take corrective action.

question: Which of the following is least likely to be a direct recommendation for safer night driving?
options: a:Carrying a flashlight in your vehicle,b:Keeping your windshield clean,c:Being aware that tinted windows reduce nighttime visibility
