note: While a flashlight can be useful if stranded, key safe night-driving practices include keeping the windshield clean and recognizing that tinted windows reduce nighttime visibility.

question: Which is a safe way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.,b:Speed up entering the curve and slow down as you exit.,c:Maintain maximum speed throughout the curve.
note: Reduce speed before a curve and accelerate gradually as you exit to maintain control through the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the usual speed limit in a school zone unless otherwise posted?
options: a:25 mph.,b:15 mph.,c:30 mph.,d:20 mph.
note: Unless signs specify otherwise, the speed limit in a school zone is the same as residential/business zones: 25 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle that honks first.,d:The faster vehicle.
note: When vehicles arrive at the same time at an intersection without signals, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with working lights, what should you do?
options: a:Follow the officer's directions,b:Obey the traffic lights instead,c:Ignore both and proceed,d:Sound your horn
note: An officer's directions override traffic signals and signs; obey the officer when directing traffic.

question: What characterizes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Anticipates the actions of other drivers,b:Always drives slowly regardless of conditions,c:Never changes speed,d:Relies exclusively on other drivers to be cautious
note: A defensive driver watches for others' actions, anticipates hazards, and adjusts driving to reduce risk.

question: Does vehicle speed affect stopping distance?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: The faster your speed, the longer the distance and time required to stop or react to unexpected situations.

question: If stopped by a police officer, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the wheel and wait for the officer.,b:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window before they reach you.,c:Exit the vehicle immediately and approach the officer.,d:Retrieve your documents before the officer arrives
note: Remain inside unless asked to exit; keep hands visible and wait for the officer to request your license, registration, and insurance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When anything makes conditions less than perfect,b:Only when you see a police officer,c:When entering a highway where there are other cars
note: Drive below the posted limit whenever conditions (weather, visibility, road surface, traffic) make the posted limit unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds.,b:Slow speeds.,c:Night driving.,d:Low tire pressure
note: Higher speeds dramatically increase stopping distances and the severity of collisions.

question: Must you yield to children playing in the street?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drive with extra caution in residential areas, playgrounds and near schools, and yield to children when present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, what should you do with your speed?
options: a:Reduce your speed to maintain control.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Maintain or vary as you like.,d:Come to a stop and then accelerate speedily
note: Slow to a speed that lets you control the vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to unexpected hazards while turning.

question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates what?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to change lanes over the line,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid line discourages or prohibits lane changes; yellow lines divide opposing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond when you see a yield sign at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and yield to traffic in the road you are entering.,b:Always come to a complete stop regardless of traffic.,c:Yield only to traffic on your left.,d:Proceed without slowing if no traffic is visible
note: At a yield sign, slow and give right-of-way to vehicles or pedestrians in the roadway you are entering; stop if necessary.

question: Lack of sleep affects your driving similar to which of the following?
options: a:The effect that alcohol has,b:The effect that amphetamines have,c:The effect that anger has
note: Fatigue impairs driving ability similarly to alcohol: for example, being awake 18 hours can impair driving about as much as a BAC of 0.05 percent, and 24 hours similar to 0.10 percent.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when a traffic signal shows a steady red arrow?
options: a:Come to a full stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,b:Slow and proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Stop, then proceed when the way is clear.,d:Turn immediately if no pedestrians are present.
note: A red arrow requires drivers to stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow is displayed, unless a sign indicates otherwise.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.,b:Getting ahead of poor drivers to stay safe.,c:Following closely to prevent cut-offs.,d:Driving only during daylight hours
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards and taking action to prevent conflicts and accidents.

question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
options: a:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.,b:Slam on your brakes to scare them away.,c:Speed up to increase distance from them.,d:Ignore them and maintain speed
note: Safely change lanes or gradually reduce speed to let the tailgater pass rather than engaging in aggressive actions.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A reflective orange triangle,b:A rectangular red sign,c:A circular green sign
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle indicating a vehicle is traveling 25 mph or less; use caution when approaching.

question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks for a short time when moving with a stream of vehicles?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Do not stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Only cross when there is room on the far side for your entire vehicle so you will not be stopped on the tracks.

question: What must a professional truck driver have to operate commercial vehicles?
options: a:A valid commercial driver's license (CDL),b:Ownership of an 18-wheeler,c:A fishing license,d:A regular driver's license only
note: Operating large commercial vehicles requires a valid CDL; a regular license is not sufficient for many commercial vehicles.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:As a stop sign—come to a complete stop,b:Proceed without stopping if no traffic is present,c:Ignore it,d:Only stop if police are present
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop; proceed only when safe.

question: In Virginia, when transporting anyone under 18, what must the driver ensure?
options: a:All passengers under 18 are properly secured by seat belts or child safety seats,b:Only front-seat passengers under 18 must be belted,c:Only passengers under 8 must be belted,d:It is the passenger's responsibility
note: Drivers are responsible for ensuring passengers under 18 are properly secured, no matter where they are seated.

question: When dealing with pedestrians, what is a driver's responsibility?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians and do everything possible to avoid striking them,b:Require pedestrians to always yield,c:Only watch for pedestrians at marked crosswalks,d:Yell at pedestrians to stay out of the road
note: Drivers must be alert and yield to pedestrians, doing everything possible to prevent collisions, even if pedestrians are not where they should be.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing where you see no train, when must you still stop?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted,b:If crossing gate is lowered or lights are flashing,c:If a flagger signals you to stop,d:All of the above
note: Stop when flashing lights are active, gates are down, a stop sign is posted, a flagger orders you to stop, or a train is visible and close.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're traveling slower than other traffic on a multilane roadway, you must:
options: a:Drive in the right-hand lane.,b:Stay in the middle lane.,c:Not change lanes.
note: On multilane roads, slower vehicles should remain in the right-hand lane to allow faster traffic to pass on the left.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to exceed the speed limit when passing another vehicle?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must obey the posted speed limit at all times; it is illegal to exceed it even when passing another vehicle.

question: When should you slow down?
options: a:When the road is wet or slippery,b:Only when a police car is present,c:When entering a highway with other cars
note: Reduce speed on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and crossings, on hills and curves, where pedestrians are present, and when roads are wet or slippery.

question: If a railroad crossing has no warning devices, you should slow down, look, and listen before proceeding.
options: a:True,b:False
note: At crossings without active warnings you should slow down, look both directions, and listen for trains before crossing.

question: To relieve fatigue on a long trip, which is recommended?
options: a:Stop and rest about every two hours,b:Keep driving and play loud music,c:Drive with one eye closed to rest the other,d:Only take caffeine to stay alert
note: Make regular stops to rest and stretch; if drowsy, find a safe place to rest or stay overnight.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid,b:Overcorrect the steering to regain control,c:Turn your wheel into traffic
note: If the rear of your vehicle skids, steer in the direction of the skid to regain control; remain calm and avoid abrupt corrections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:As close to the right side of the roadway as possible,b:Near the center of the street,c:Close to the left side of the street
note: Prepare for right turns by moving as far to the right as is safe and practical; do not cut across lanes when turning.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Human error,b:Bad weather,c:New drivers,d:Vehicle defects
note: Human error—such as inattention or mistakes—is the most common cause of crashes.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires the same action as which device?
options: a:A stop sign,b:A yield sign,c:A slow sign,d:A speed limit sign
note: A flashing red light means stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when safe—same as a stop sign.

question: Are motorists required to yield to pedestrians who walk against the traffic light?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the roadway, even if they are crossing against a signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are drivers required to yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Drivers must stop and yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks and to pedestrians crossing the driver’s side at unmarked crosswalks when no traffic control signals are present.

question: Where are you prohibited from parking?
options: a:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane,b:In a parking lot,c:On a hill
note: It is illegal to park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. Other prohibited areas include within specified distances of fire hydrants, intersections, and railroad crossings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind while driving uphill, what should you expect about the truck's speed?
options: a:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit,b:You may not be able to legally pass the truck,c:You may be able to pass at any time
note: Large trucks often slow on inclines and may travel below the posted speed; exercise caution and do not attempt to pass on hills with limited visibility.

question: What causes “highway hypnosis”?
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods,b:Getting frequent rest breaks,c:Too much sleep before driving
note: Highway hypnosis occurs when a driver stares straight ahead and stops actively scanning the environment, increasing the likelihood of not noticing slowing or stopped traffic ahead.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks on a busy street, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off the ignition while avoiding locking the steering, apply brakes, and move safely off the road,b:Slam on the brakes repeatedly until the engine stalls,c:Keep accelerating and hope it stops,d:Jump out of the moving vehicle
note: If the accelerator sticks, carefully turn off the ignition to stop the engine (without engaging steering lock), brake, and pull to a safe location.

question: What should be your first response to decreased visibility while driving?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers only.,c:Flash your high beams.,d:Open your windows for fresh air.
note: When visibility drops, slow down first to increase reaction time; then use lights or wipers as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection but no stop line or crosswalk is visible, where should you stop?
options: a:Stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:Slow down but do not stop unless you see cross traffic.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the nearest point before the intersection where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersecting roadway.

question: Why must you be especially careful near a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are a police officer.,b:They may be deaf.,c:They are blind or visually impaired.
note: A pedestrian with a white cane or a guide dog is blind or visually impaired; you must slow down, yield, and be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right,b:Either one may proceed first,c:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left
note: When vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the best response?
options: a:Stay calm and move out of their way,b:Flash lights and honk repeatedly,c:Retaliate by speeding up,d:Block their vehicle from passing
note: Remain calm and create distance; do not engage or retaliate to avoid escalation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When stopped in a travel lane, are you allowed to stop to drop off passengers or look up an address?
options: a:No — do not stop in a travel lane; pull off the road to do such tasks.,b:Yes — stopping in a travel lane is acceptable.,c:Only if you flash your hazards first.,d:Only during off-peak hours.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane; keep moving until you can safely pull off the roadway.

question: How should drivers treat traffic signs and pavement markings?
options: a:They must always be obeyed.,b:They are merely suggestions.,c:They apply only when other traffic is present.,d:They are optional at night
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control flow and safety and must be followed at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop before entering and verifying it is safe to proceed.,b:After slowing to check for traffic only if cars are present.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.,d:Without stopping if no pedestrians are visible
note: If no stop line or crosswalk is present, stop before entering the intersection and proceed only when it is safe.

question: At what minimum BAC are drivers 21 and older legally considered to be driving under the influence?
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.06 percent.,c:0.02 percent.,d:0.10 percent.
note: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08% or greater for drivers 21+ constitutes driving under the influence; impairment can occur below that level.

question: How should you behave when near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop,b:Proceed normally; they will yield,c:Take the right-of-way,d:Honk to alert them
note: Yield and be prepared to stop for a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog to prevent injury.

question: What is the correct top-to-bottom order of vertically arranged traffic lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Green, yellow, red.,c:Yellow, red, green.,d:Red, green, yellow
note: On vertical signals red is on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom; on horizontal signals red is at the left.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you find yourself driving in another driver's blind spot, what is the safest action?
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you,b:Remain at the same speed and position,c:Stay in the blind spot until the other driver changes lanes
note: Do not drive in another vehicle’s blind spot; adjust your position so the other driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: Which action best helps you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive,b:Simply say “No thanks, I'm driving” when offered a drink,c:Call a taxi only after you start drinking
note: Deciding ahead of time not to drive after drinking is the most reliable way to avoid driving under the influence, since alcohol impairs judgment.

question: What lane space is a motorcyclist entitled to?
options: a:Half the lane width.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:A bicycle lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane, just like other motor vehicles.

question: Do drivers need to allow the same following distance behind motorcycles as behind cars?
options: a:No—TRUE,b:Yes—FALSE,c:Only in wet conditions,d:Only at high speeds
note: Motorcycles can stop more quickly, but you should still allow at least three to four seconds of following distance for safety.

question: If a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light and you are turning, who must yield?
options: a:The driver turning must yield to the pedestrian.,b:The pedestrian must always yield.,c:The first person to move has the right-of-way.,d:The pedestrian only yields if not in a marked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing intersections even if no signal is present.

question: Which of these is NOT part of the searching technique when driving?
options: a:Trying to find your car in a parking lot,b:Looking ahead and behind for hazards,c:Checking left, then right, then left again before entering an intersection
note: Searching means scanning the driving environment for hazards (look ahead, behind, and left-right-left at intersections). Looking for your parked car is not part of this driving search technique.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to pass on a two-lane road when your side has a single solid yellow centerline?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: You may not pass when there is a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline; passing is allowed only when the broken line is on your side.

question: At an intersection, when must you stop for a traffic signal?
options: a:At a flashing red light,b:At a steady yellow light,c:At a yellow arrow,d:When a green light is flashing
note: A flashing red light means stop—treat it the same as a stop sign.

question: As a pedestrian, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Entering a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,b:Using designated crosswalks.,c:Waiting for vehicles to stop before stepping out.,d:Wearing reflective clothing at night.
note: Pedestrians should not enter crosswalks or roadways when approaching vehicles may not have time to stop.

question: Is it lawful to use only parking lights while driving at night?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must use headlights when driving at night; parking lights alone are not permitted for nighttime driving.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is moving?
options: a:No — you must not drive around or under a lowering or raising gate,b:Yes, if an approaching train is not close,c:Yes, if you first look carefully in both directions
note: You must never drive around or under crossing gates. Wait until lights stop, bells are silent, and gates are fully raised before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions.,b:The posted maximum speed only, regardless of conditions.,c:The speed that makes you feel safe.,d:Always at or below 25 mph.
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for the current conditions, not just the posted limit.

question: How are bicycles classified under traffic law?
options: a:Considered vehicles and have the same rights as motor vehicles,b:Required to stay on sidewalks,c:Considered vehicles but without the same rights as motor vehicles
note: Bicycles are vehicles and cyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers, except where prohibited (e.g., interstate highways).

question: Is it illegal to use a radar detector in Virginia?
options: a:Yes—TRUE,b:No—FALSE,c:Only in commercial vehicles,d:Only at night
note: Virginia law prohibits the use of radar detectors in motor vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady green light, what should a driver do?
options: a:Continue driving unless pedestrians or vehicles are already in the intersection.,b:Stop if you see a police officer nearby.,c:Treat it as a four-way stop.
note: On a steady green you may proceed, but yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection and be prepared to stop if the light changes.

question: When stopped for a violation or equipment check, what documents must a driver produce?
options: a:Driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.,b:Only a driver's license.,c:Only proof of insurance.,d:No documents are required to be produced.
note: Drivers must present license, registration, and insurance when stopped for violations or checks.

question: If someone is injured in an accident, what should you do?
options: a:Move the injured away from the scene immediately.,b:Always leave the injured where they are.,c:Avoid moving the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid.
note: Do not move an injured person unnecessarily; keep them warm and administer first aid if you are able until professional help arrives.

question: What is the risk of eating or drinking while driving?
options: a:It creates distractions that reduce control and lane-keeping,b:It makes you a better driver because you are not hungry,c:It has no effect,d:It improves reaction time
note: Eating or drinking takes hands and eyes off driving tasks, making lane control and reaction slower.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill next to a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb
note: When parked uphill with a curb, set the parking brake and turn your wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low-beam headlights,b:Parking lights,c:High-beam headlights
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

question: How should you treat railroad crossings?
options: a:Safe to park near.,b:Safe to cross; trains rarely come.,c:Dangerous; always look and listen.
note: Railroad crossings are potentially dangerous; always look and listen for trains and obey signs, signals, and flaggers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From the center left-turn lane, which maneuvers are typically allowed?
options: a:You may make left turns from either direction.,b:You may pass slower vehicles.,c:You may make U-turns at any time.,d:You may drive straight through the intersection
note: Center left-turn lanes are reserved for vehicles making left turns from either direction and are not for passing or through traffic.

question: If taking an over-the-counter medication, how should you approach driving?
options: a:Read the label for warnings and ask a doctor or pharmacist if unsure.,b:Mix it with alcohol to increase effectiveness.,c:Assume it has no effect and drive as usual.,d:Only drive if you feel fine after taking it.
note: Many nonprescription medicines can impair driving; check labels or consult a professional before driving.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a:If you are both traveling on a two-lane highway and the bus's red lights are flashing,b:When it approaches you even if its lights are not flashing,c:If it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it
note: You must stop when approaching a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights on a two-lane roadway; traffic in both directions must stop and remain stopped until the lights are off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Toward the curb (right), so the vehicle rolls toward the curb if it moves.,b:Toward the center of the road (left).,c:Keep wheels straight ahead.,d:Turn wheels sharply to the left and leave the car in neutral.
note: Turn wheels toward the curb on a downhill slope so a rolling vehicle will move away from traffic.

question: Which behavior helps prevent crashes by improving communication with others?
options: a:Using signals and other cues to communicate intentions.,b:Ignoring other drivers to concentrate on yourself.,c:Driving only on side streets to avoid traffic.,d:Hiding your intentions until the last moment.
note: Use turn signals, brake lights, and horn when appropriate to let other road users know your intentions.

question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, what is required?
options: a:Drive to the right and stop until it passes,b:Slow down but stay in your lane,c:Signal it to pass,d:Ignore it if you are in a hurry
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by immediately driving to the right and stopping until they have passed; if in an intersection, clear it then stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection's traffic signals are out due to a power outage, you should:
options: a:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and proceed when it is your turn.,b:Drive through without stopping if you think it's clear.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and continue without stopping.,d:Ignore other vehicles and proceed quickly.
note: When traffic lights are out, drivers should yield as at a four-way stop and proceed cautiously when it is their turn.

question: Is it legal to drive at night using only your parking lights?
options: a:No — this is unlawful.,b:Yes, it is acceptable everywhere.,c:Only if you are in a well-lit area.,d:Only during emergencies.
note: Drivers must use headlights when driving at night; parking lights alone are not sufficient.

question: What do round traffic signs indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:No passing zones.,c:Railroad crossings ahead.
note: Round signs warn of an approaching railroad crossing; exercise extra caution when you see them.

question: If involved in an accident, what are your immediate responsibilities?
options: a:Stop, help the injured, and call police if necessary,b:Leave the scene if no one appears hurt,c:Move injured people immediately without assessing them,d:Only exchange insurance information and leave
note: Stop your vehicle, assist injured persons as appropriate without moving them unnecessarily, and call law enforcement or emergency services.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you required to signal every time you pull away from a curb?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must use your turn signal whenever you pull away from a curb or change position on the roadway to inform other drivers.

question: When you first encounter rain while driving, what is the safe action?
options: a:Slow down,b:Drive faster to clear the area more quickly,c:Increase your following distance but maintain speed
note: When rain begins and visibility or traction is reduced, slow down, turn on headlights, and increase following distance; pull off if visibility becomes unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an acceleration ramp, who must yield?
options: a:The driver entering the interstate must yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:Drivers on the interstate must always slow down.,c:The entering driver has the right-of-way.,d:Both must stop before merging
note: Drivers accelerating onto an interstate should yield to traffic already on the highway and merge only when safe.

question: If involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what are your immediate responsibilities?
options: a:Stop, determine if anyone is injured, and call the police if necessary.,b:Leave the scene quickly if you are not at fault.,c:Only call your insurance company and drive away.,d:Move victims without checking for injuries first
note: Stop and, if possible, move to safety; check for injuries and call 911 for medical emergencies or if reportable damage thresholds are met.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop, creating a clear path for the emergency vehicle,b:Stop immediately where you are without checking surroundings,c:Speed up to get out of the way,d:Turn on hazard lights and continue slowly
note: Safely move to the right and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass; if in heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can get out of the way.

question: Does paying the $500 uninsured motor vehicle fee provide liability insurance coverage?
options: a:Yes,b:No
note: The $500 uninsured motor vehicle fee does not provide insurance; it only allows vehicle registration under certain conditions.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?
options: a:Follow the flagger's directions,b:Do what the surrounding traffic does despite the flagger,c:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be there
note: Flaggers are authorized to control traffic in work zones; obey their directions for the safety of workers and road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass,b:Decrease your speed even further,c:Not let other cars pass your vehicle
note: If you are impeding the normal flow of traffic on a two-lane road, you should safely pull off and allow other vehicles to pass.

question: Before changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Signal in advance and check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
note: Signal early, check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open (uncontrolled) intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right,b:The driver on the left,c:Either driver may proceed without yielding
note: When two vehicles arrive to an open intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right. Proceed only when safe.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:When passing another car.,b:When you have to stop quickly.,c:When you lose control of your car to warn others.
note: One appropriate use of the horn is to alert others if you lose control or to warn of an immediate danger.

question: When other drivers around you are acting angrily, how should you respond?
options: a:Distance yourself from them and avoid eye contact,b:React with hand gestures to show you are not intimidated,c:Make eye contact to try to calm them
note: If a driver is behaving aggressively, put distance between you and them, avoid eye contact and gestures, and do what you can safely to get out of the situation.

question: What is the DMV's vision standard for an unrestricted driver license?
options: a:20/40 or better vision in one or both eyes,b:20/20 or better in one or both eyes,c:20/60 or better vision in one or both eyes
note: An unrestricted Virginia driver license requires 20/40 or better vision in one or both eyes and approximately 110 degrees horizontal field of vision in one or both eyes (or comparable field measurement).

question: When should you use turn signals or hand signals?
options: a:When making turns,b:When changing lanes,c:When entering or exiting highways,d:All of the above
note: Use signals whenever you plan to turn, change lanes, or enter/exit a highway to communicate with others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp regarding speed?
options: a:Slow down once you have moved onto the exit ramp,b:Slow down before you enter the exit ramp,c:Keep your speed constant on the ramp
note: Do not start braking on the freeway; wait until you have moved onto the exit ramp, then reduce speed to the advisory or posted ramp speed.

question: What should drivers know about large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles,c:They need less space to turn,d:They are easier to overtake in curves
note: Large trucks have big blind spots and require more distance to maneuver and stop; avoid lingering near them.

question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep tires properly inflated and with good tread, and reduce speed in the rain.,b:Increase speed in heavy rain.,c:Use underinflated tires to increase traction.,d:Drive with cruise control on
note: Good tire tread, correct tire pressure, and reduced speed during rain lower hydroplaning risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light turns yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Begin slowing and be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so.,c:Stop abruptly in the center of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns the signal will change to red; slow down and prepare to stop if it is safe.

question: On slippery roads, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed and avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,c:Always drive at the posted maximum speed.
note: Reduce speed, avoid sudden maneuvers, and do not use cruise control on slippery surfaces.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road with opposing traffic, when should you return to the driving lane?
options: a:When there is enough room between you and the vehicle passed.,b:Immediately after passing regardless of distance.,c:Only after the passed vehicle signals.,d:When you reach the next mile marker
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What best ensures safety when you are about to back your vehicle?
options: a:Check behind the vehicle on foot before getting into the driver's seat,b:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse,c:Check your rearview mirrors only
note: Before backing, walk to the rear of the vehicle to check for children, pets, or obstacles; then use mirrors and backup cameras as available.

question: Where should you try to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:On all sides of your vehicle.,b:Only in front of the vehicle.,c:Only behind your vehicle.,d:Only to the left and right of your vehicle
note: Maintain space on all sides to give yourself time to react to hazards and to maneuver safely.

question: What typically causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Driving too fast for wet road conditions so tires cannot clear water.,b:Excessive stops.,c:Sudden stops.,d:Old windshield wipers
note: At higher speeds, tires can lose contact with the road surface over a thin layer of water, causing hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when approaching a steady yellow traffic light?
options: a:Slow to a stop unless you are already in the intersection.,b:Accelerate to beat the red light.,c:Assume you have right-of-way and continue.,d:Stop abruptly in the lane
note: A steady yellow warns a red is coming; you should stop if it is safe to do so, unless you are already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where are U-turns allowed in business districts, cities, and towns?
options: a:Only at intersections,b:Anywhere on the roadway,c:Only on highways,d:Only in parking lots
note: In business districts, cities, and towns, U-turns are permitted only at intersections unless otherwise posted.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Increase speed to clear the tracks,b:Slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop,c:Drive across without stopping if you do not see a train,d:Sound your horn and proceed
note: When you approach a railroad crossing, slow down, look both ways for trains, and be prepared to stop if needed.

question: Under what circumstances can DMV deny or suspend driving privileges for persons under 18?
options: a:If the juvenile is found delinquent by a court or involved in alcohol/drug-related offenses.,b:If the juvenile misses school occasionally.,c:If the juvenile lacks parental supervision but has no offenses.,d:If the juvenile is under 21
note: DMV may suspend or deny driving privileges for juveniles adjudicated delinquent or involved in alcohol/drug-related offenses or certain traffic violations.

question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When the entire passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror,b:When your front bumper aligns with the other's rear bumper,c:When you feel it is safe,d:When the other driver signals you to return
note: Return to your lane only after you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

question: Regulatory signs are usually what color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:White,b:Blue,c:Green,d:Yellow
note: Regulatory signs are typically white with black lettering and must be obeyed, as they control traffic movement.

question: How does increasing your speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It decreases your field of vision,b:It increases your field of vision,c:It has no effect,d:It makes peripheral vision better
note: As speed increases, your effective field of vision narrows, so you must be more alert for hazards.

question: What do pentagonal road signs indicate?
options: a:School zones and school crossings,b:No passing zones,c:Speed limits,d:Railroad crossings
note: Pentagonal (five-sided) signs warn you that you are in a school zone or near a school crossing.

question: Which of the following about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:It is illegal to go around lowered gates, and not all crossings have signals.,b:You may always go around gates if no train is visible.,c:All crossings have flashing signals and gates.,d:You never have to stop at a crossing directed by a flagger.
note: Some crossings lack signals; however, going around lowered gates is illegal and flaggers must be obeyed.

question: Should you use high beams when driving in fog?
options: a:Yes—TRUE,b:No—FALSE,c:Use only if there are no other vehicles,d:Use parking lights instead
note: High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility; use low beams or fog lights instead.

question: Why is it important to be alert to motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and harder to see than cars,b:They rarely use headlights,c:Motorcyclists are less skilled,d:They always drive at the speed limit
note: Motorcycles are smaller, easier to hide in blind spots, and harder to judge for distance and speed, so be especially cautious.

question: What do your brake lights signal to drivers behind you?
options: a:You are slowing down or stopping.,b:You are making a turn.,c:You have your emergency brake on.
note: Brake lights indicate to vehicles behind you that you are slowing down or stopping and should be in working order.

question: Anything that causes you to ____ can lead to a crash.
options: a:Take your attention away from driving.,b:Drive at the posted speed limit.,c:Use your turn signal.,d:Check mirrors regularly.
note: Distractions that take your eyes, hands, or attention away from driving increase crash risk.

question: What is the most important rule for managing speed when approaching a curve?
options: a:Slow down before you enter the curve,b:Drive at the posted speed as you enter then brake at the sharpest part,c:Accelerate gently as you enter the curve
note: Vehicles tend to continue straight due to inertia; reduce speed before entering a curve to maintain control and avoid having to brake hard mid-curve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when turning or changing lanes?
options: a:Always signal your intentions, even if no traffic is visible.,b:Signal only when other traffic is present.,c:Signal only at night.,d:Signal only on highways
note: You must signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Make signaling a habit regardless of visible traffic.

question: When a transit bus signals to merge back into traffic after stopping, you must:
options: a:Yield to allow the bus to re-enter safely.,b:Speed up to pass the bus before it merges.,c:Honk to alert the driver.,d:Ignore the bus's signal and maintain speed.
note: Drivers should yield by changing lanes, slowing, or stopping to let the transit vehicle merge safely.

question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee and rest.,b:Exercise to sweat it out.,c:Allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.
note: The only effective way to reduce BAC is to allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol; coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not reduce BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a prohibited passing situation?
options: a:When a solid line marks the left side of your lane,b:When a school bus is stopped to load/unload on a public road without a physical barrier,c:When passing requires leaving the paved roadway,d:All of the above
note: Do not pass when a solid centerline is next to your lane, when a school bus is stopped loading/unloading (unless separated), or by leaving the pavement.

question: When parking next to a curb, what is the maximum distance from the curb you may park?
options: a:6 inches,b:12 inches (one foot),c:18 inches,d:2 feet
note: On public roads you may not park more than one foot from the curb.

question: To avoid driving unsafely due to health or medication, you should:
options: a:Drive within your physical limitations.,b:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,c:Ignore medicine warnings if you feel fine.
note: Know how your health and any medicines affect your driving and operate the vehicle only within your physical capabilities.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady red traffic light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop,b:Continue through if no other traffic is present,c:Slow down and proceed with caution
note: A steady red light requires a complete stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, or before entering the intersection; you may turn right after stopping unless prohibited.

question: If you intend to move from the right lane to the left on a multilane highway, what should you check?
options: a:Look over your left shoulder to check the blind spot, and check mirrors before signaling.,b:Only check the rearview mirror.,c:Turn on your signal and immediately change lanes.,d:Sound your horn and change lanes quickly
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, glance over your shoulder into the blind spot in the direction of the move, and signal.

question: Which headlights should you use in the rain?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.,d:Emergency flashers.
note: Use low beams in rainy conditions to reduce glare and improve visibility for yourself and others.

question: If railroad crossing signals are flashing as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Stop well back (no closer than 15 feet) and wait for the train to pass.,b:Slow down and cross quickly before the train arrives.,c:Proceed cautiously without stopping.,d:Drive around lowered gates if no train is visible.
note: If lights are flashing or gates are down, stop at a safe distance and only cross once it is clear and safe.

question: If a fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but is not using its emergency lights or siren, how should you respond?
options: a:Continue driving in a normal manner,b:Stop as quickly as possible,c:Speed up to get out of its way
note: If an emergency vehicle is not using lights and siren, you do not need to clear the roadway; continue driving normally. Only when emergency signals are used must you yield.

question: What is the shape of a stop sign?
options: a:Octagon,b:Rectangle,c:Circle,d:Diamond
note: Stop signs use an eight-sided (octagonal) shape to indicate a full stop is required.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Stop driving and rest,b:Get some coffee and keep going,c:Open your window to stay alert
note: Fatigue impairs driving similar to alcohol. If you feel tired, stop driving, rest, or switch drivers rather than continuing.

question: Must you use headlights whenever you use windshield wipers because of weather?
options: a:True,b:False
note: In Virginia you must use headlights anytime windshield wipers are needed due to weather conditions to increase visibility.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and driving?
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem.,b:A minor traffic issue.,c:Safe if you have had only a few drinks.,d:Not a problem for experienced drivers
note: Driving after drinking or using drugs is dangerous and greatly impairs driving ability, endangering you and others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an uncontrolled intersection, what is the correct action?
options: a:Stop, check all directions, and then proceed when safe,b:Maintain your speed and proceed without checking,c:Yield to all other drivers regardless of their position
note: At uncontrolled intersections, slow, cover the brake, check left-right-left, and yield to traffic on your right if they arrived first.

question: Which statement about changing weather and driving is correct?
options: a:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.,b:Always increase your speed in rain.,c:Ignore vehicles behind you in bad weather.
note: If the weather changes suddenly, you must adapt your driving (slow down in rain or fog and be aware of vehicles behind you).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is trying to pass your car, how should you respond?
options: a:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.,b:Pull off the road immediately.,c:Signal them when it is safe for them to pass.,d:Speed up to prevent them from passing
note: Stay in your lane, check for oncoming vehicles, and adjust speed if necessary to allow the overtaking vehicle to complete its pass safely.

question: If children are playing near your driveway and you need to back out, what should you do before moving?
options: a:Get out and walk to the rear of the car to ensure the way is clear,b:Sound your horn to warn them,c:Rev your engine to alert them,d:Back out slowly relying on mirrors only
note: Before backing into or out of a driveway near children, exit the vehicle and check behind it rather than relying solely on mirrors.

question: Which steps should you take when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Signal, check rearview and side mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots,b:Only signal and change lanes quickly,c:Rely solely on your mirrors,d:Only change lanes if other drivers wave you
note: Signal early, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to verify blind spots before changing lanes.

question: When driving on wet pavement, what should you remember?
options: a:Pavement is especially slippery just after it starts raining,b:Wet roads can cause hydroplaning,c:Give extra stopping distance,d:All of the above
note: Roads can be especially slick at the onset of rain; wet surfaces increase hydroplaning risk and require extra stopping distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Slow down and change lanes away from it if possible.,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.,c:Drive to the right and stop.
note: When approaching a stopped emergency, tow, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes away if safe; otherwise slow down and give space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street, which lane should you begin from?
options: a:The left lane,b:The middle lane,c:The right lane,d:Any lane works
note: When turning left from a multilane one-way street or highway, start from the left lane.

question: Is it true that drivers should avoid staying beside large vehicles for long periods because of their blind spots?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Large vehicles have big blind spots on both sides; avoid driving alongside them for long periods and pass promptly and safely.

question: What is the most common mistake drivers make when backing?
options: a:True — failing to look both ways behind them.,b:False — mirrors are always sufficient.,c:True — relying on a backup camera only.
note: Many drivers fail to turn and look both ways through the rear window when backing; mirrors do not show everything.

question: Does a 'Merging lanes' sign mean drivers should be prepared to change lanes or allow others to merge?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A 'Merging lanes' sign warns that two lanes will merge and drivers should be ready to change lanes or allow traffic to merge.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which actions should you take before changing lanes?
options: a:Use your turn signal, check side and rearview mirrors, and check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.,b:Signal only, then change lanes.,c:Check your blind spot only, then change lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder for vehicles in your blind spots and for drivers also changing lanes.

question: Which of the following summarizes your responsibilities each time you drive?
options: a:Accept responsibility for your actions and obey Virginia traffic laws.,b:Assume others will always yield to you.,c:Drive only when accompanied.,d:Ignore traffic laws if roads are empty.
note: Every time you drive you must accept responsibility, obey laws, and work to keep everyone safe.

question: When must you remain stopped for a school bus with flashing signals and the stop arm extended?
options: a:Until all children are clear of the roadway and the bus moves again.,b:Until the bus driver waves you by.,c:Until the red lights stop flashing even if children remain near the bus.,d:Only if you are driving in the same direction as the bus
note: Stop for school buses on any roadway when red lights flash and the stop arm is extended; remain stopped until children are clear and the bus moves.

question: Which of the following does NOT normally occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:You are more alert,b:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down,c:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted
note: Alcohol reduces alertness, slows reaction time, and distorts judgment of speed and distance; becoming more alert is not an effect of drinking.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and you may change lanes when safe.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and you may pass.,d:Do not change lanes under any circumstances.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes going the same way; crossing is allowed when safe to change lanes or pass.

question: What driving habit can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Slowing down gradually and avoiding sudden stops,b:Accelerating quickly from stops,c:Idling in driveways with the engine running,d:Frequent hard braking
note: Looking ahead and slowing gradually reduces unnecessary braking and acceleration, improving fuel economy.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Drive as far to the right as possible and stop,b:Stop immediately where you are without moving,c:Drive slowly and let it pass on your left,d:Speed up to get out of the way
note: On a two-lane or undivided road, pull to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass safely.

question: Combining alcohol with drugs can cause what effect?
options: a:Increase the effects of both substances,b:Reduce the effects making them safe,c:Have no interaction,d:Prevent impairment entirely
note: Alcohol can interact with drugs to amplify impairment and increase danger when driving.

question: What is the 'No zone' in relation to trucks and buses?
options: a:Blind spots around a truck or bus where the vehicle cannot see you.,b:A speed enforcement area for trucks.,c:A restricted parking zone.,d:A quiet zone near schools
note: The 'No zone' describes the large blind spots on trucks and buses where smaller vehicles may be invisible to the truck driver.

question: When children are playing nearby, what should you expect them to do?
options: a:Run into the street without looking.,b:Stop at the curb before crossing.,c:Always know when it is safe to cross.,d:Obey crossing guards reliably
note: Reduce speed and exercise extra caution; children may act unpredictably and may run into the roadway without looking.

question: What is the safest location to install a child safety seat in a car?
options: a:The center of the back seat,b:The front passenger seat,c:The driver's side back seat
note: The center of the rear seat is generally the safest location for a child safety seat because it provides the greatest distance from potential collision points.

question: When driving near light rail vehicles, which precaution should you always take?
options: a:Expect trains on any track at any time,b:Ignore posted signs if no train is visible,c:Assume you have the right-of-way at all crossings
note: Near light rail systems, expect trains on any track at any time, obey signage and signals, and only cross when you can clear the tracks without stopping on them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, who yields?
options: a:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:The car on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The car on the left shall yield to the car on the right.
note: If two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: About how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer be able to travel before stopping from 55 mph?
options: a:50 feet,b:125 feet,c:400 feet.
note: Large tractor-trailers require substantially greater stopping distances; at 55 mph a fully loaded truck may need nearly 400 feet to stop.

question: When stopping on an uphill slope, when should you increase your space cushion?
options: a:On an incline.,b:At an intersection.,c:At a stop sign.
note: Allow extra space when stopped on an uphill slope because the vehicle ahead could roll back when traffic resumes.

question: Which actions can lead to your license being revoked or suspended?
options: a:Making a false statement to the DMV.,b:Driving with a broken taillight.,c:Running out of fuel on the highway.,d:Parking in a no-parking zone
note: The DMV or courts can suspend or revoke licenses for crimes such as making false statements to the DMV, eluding police, or taking an exam for another person.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely,b:Speed up to pass in front of them,c:Honk to make them move,d:Proceed because you have the right-of-way
note: Yield to pedestrians and any vehicles in the intersection; stop if necessary to allow them to cross safely.

question: Do large vehicles have blind spots that can extend far behind them?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Large trucks and buses have significant blind spots, including an area directly behind that can extend a considerable distance; avoid tailgating them.

question: What happens if you take drugs along with alcohol?
options: a:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,b:It lessens the effect of alcohol.,c:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,d:It neutralizes alcohol impairment
note: Combining alcohol with medications or drugs increases impairment and the risk of a crash.

question: What are the consequences of driving in Virginia without liability insurance?
options: a:Suspension of your driver license and a $500 fee until you provide proof of insurance.,b:A small warning with no financial penalty.,c:Only higher premiums later.,d:No consequences if you pay later
note: Drivers caught without required insurance must pay a $500 fee, submit proof of proper coverage, and may face license suspension until compliance.

question: How should you treat a railroad crossbuck sign?
options: a:Like a yield sign — yield to any oncoming trains.,b:As a stop sign always.,c:As an advisory only that you may ignore if no train is visible.,d:As a pedestrian-only crossing sign
note: A crossbuck indicates you must yield the right-of-way to trains and not cross if a train is approaching.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:When you see flashing lights or hear a siren.,b:Only if they are behind you.,c:Never — emergency vehicles must avoid you.,d:Only if a police officer tells you to do so.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to vehicles using audible or visual emergency signals.

question: What is the most effective action to lower your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Wear your seat belt.,b:Stay in the right lane on highways.,c:Drive only on weekdays.,d:Keep windows open
note: Wearing a seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce injury or death in a crash.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, mixed drinks) change how alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Different beverage types have the same effect; only the amount matters,b:Beer affects you less than wine,c:Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you most
note: Alcohol's impairing effects depend on how much alcohol enters the bloodstream, not on the beverage type; any alcoholic beverage can impair reflexes and judgment.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicates you should:
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line on your side means passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: Is increasing your vehicle's speed the best way to avoid loss of control in wet conditions?
options: a:False,b:True
note: To avoid hydroplaning and loss of control on wet roads, reduce speed; increasing speed increases the risk of hydroplaning.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using its siren and lights, drivers must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way and follow any loudspeaker instructions.,b:Continue at the same speed and ignore the vehicle.,c:Accelerate to clear the area immediately.,d:Stop in the travel lane and wait for it to pass.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles and follow any instructions; they may operate in groups.

question: Is it lawful to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Motorcyclists are entitled to a full lane; never share a lane with a motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a “Merging traffic” sign on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles and move over a lane if safe,b:Always remain at your present speed,c:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them
note: When you see merging traffic, adjust speed and, if possible and safe, change lanes to allow entering vehicles to merge smoothly.

question: How can you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder to the side you intend to move into.,b:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Use only the outside mirror on the same side.,d:Trust lane-assist systems without looking
note: Turn your head to quickly check the blind spot before every lane change rather than relying solely on mirrors.

question: When it starts to sleet or snow while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase following distance,b:Keep normal following distance,c:Speed up to get through the area faster,d:Turn off windshield wipers to avoid streaks
note: Clear visibility is essential in sleet or snow; keep windows clear and allow extra following distance for longer stopping.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, what should drivers do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.,b:Honk before passing on the left.,c:Pass cautiously if you think children are done.,d:Slow down and pass on the right
note: When a school bus displays its stop arm and flashing red lights, drivers must stop and remain stopped until it is safe to proceed.

question: Which of these can be a sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Weaving between lanes,b:Driving more slowly than traffic,c:Making quick and sudden stops,d:All of the above
note: Signs of impairment include weaving, driving slower or faster than traffic, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

question: Should you use low-beam headlights when driving in fog?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog; high beams can reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: A downward-pointing triangular traffic sign generally means:
options: a:Yield — give way to other traffic.,b:School zone ahead.,c:Construction ahead.,d:No passing zone.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the standard yield sign shape; yield when required.

question: Where are stop lines painted on the roadway?
options: a:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks,b:On hills and curves,c:Next to churches and schools,d:At highway exits only
note: Stop lines are solid white lines across lanes at intersections and crosswalks marking where vehicles must stop.

question: When an emergency vehicle displays flashing red or blue lights, what should you do?
options: a:Pull over to the side and stop,b:Try to finish your trip before stopping,c:Continue driving but stay out of its way,d:Yell at the driver to pass
note: Yield to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens by safely pulling to the right and stopping if possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions,b:Only a recommended speed,c:The exact speed you must travel to avoid a ticket
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum legal speed for ideal conditions; you must reduce speed when conditions make the posted limit unsafe.

question: When are you required to have your headlights on?
options: a:Whenever you use your windshield wipers due to weather.,b:Only at sunset.,c:Only in clear daylight.
note: You must use headlights from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather, including anytime you use windshield wipers because of weather.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal indicate?
options: a:The protected turning movement is ending and you should prepare to stop.,b:You may turn without yielding under any circumstances.,c:The signal is malfunctioning.,d:No turning is permitted for any vehicles.
note: A solid yellow arrow is a warning that the protected turn phase is ending; prepare to stop or yield.

question: Which of these is a common cause of distracted driving?
options: a:Changing a radio station or CD.,b:Talking or texting on a cellular phone.,c:Eating, drinking, or smoking.
note: Distracted driving can be caused by many tasks, including using a phone; texting and talking on a handheld device are major distractions.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger compartment and cause poisoning.,b:It only causes minor noise issues.,c:It improves fuel efficiency.,d:It increases tire wear.
note: Exhaust leaks can let carbon monoxide and other toxic fumes enter the vehicle, posing severe health risks.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey indicated instructions are called what?
options: a:Regulatory signs,b:Warning signs,c:Information signs
note: Regulatory signs (such as speed limits, stop, and yield) inform drivers of traffic laws and regulations and must be obeyed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When visibility is reduced to 500 feet or less due to fog, what must you do about headlights?
options: a:Use low beam headlights,b:Drive without headlights,c:Use high beam headlights,d:Use only parking lights
note: Use low beam headlights (or fog lights if equipped) when visibility is reduced; high beams can worsen visibility.

question: If a solid white edge line on the right slants left toward the center, what does that indicate?
options: a:The road narrows ahead,b:There is an intersection ahead,c:You must turn left ahead,d:A passing zone begins
note: An edge line that angles toward the center signals that the road becomes narrower ahead.

question: What does an octagonal road sign always indicate?
options: a:Stop.,b:Speed limit.,c:Yield.,d:Hospital ahead
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign always means stop; you must come to a complete stop at the sign.

question: Which actions reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Do not speed on wet roads.,b:Ignore tire tread wear.,c:Drive faster to reduce contact time with water.,d:Use cruise control in heavy rain
note: Hydroplaning risk is reduced by slowing on wet roads and maintaining proper tire air pressure and tread depth.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Hold down the brake pedal.,b:Firmly pump your brakes.,c:Lightly tap the brake pedal.
note: In a non-ABS vehicle, firmly pumping the brakes can help you stop quickly while retaining some steering control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:Yes,b:No,c:Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Crossing double solid yellow lines to pass is prohibited; you may only cross to make a permitted left turn into or from a driveway or alley.

question: Because motorcycles are smaller, what should you do when pulling out into traffic?
options: a:Use extra caution before pulling out in front of a motorcycle,b:Never drive in a motorcyclist's lane,c:Always try to share a lane with a motorcycle
note: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to judge; check twice and use caution before pulling out in front of them, and never try to share the same lane with a motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is on your side, when may you pass?
options: a:When traffic is clear.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:Only on expressways.,d:Never
note: If the broken line is adjacent to your lane, you may cross to pass when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway with double solid yellow lines, you may:
options: a:Cross only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross to pass slower traffic when no oncoming traffic is present.,c:Never cross under any circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross only to make permitted left turns into or from driveways or alleys.

question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what should you do beforehand?
options: a:Plan your route in advance,b:Rely only on road signs,c:Drive without preparation,d:Only bring a cell phone
note: Plan your trip ahead of time and consult a map or directions before driving in unfamiliar areas to reduce distractions and errors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.,b:Stop and make a U-turn on the highway.,c:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,d:Signal and reverse to the exit
note: Never back up or attempt to turn around on the highway; continue to the next exit and safely return to your destination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is a situation where you should not attempt to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On a hill or curve.,b:Only when traffic is heavy.,c:When passing on a freeway with multiple lanes.
note: Never pass where your view is obstructed by a hill or curve, at intersections, or in other no-passing zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane road, you should not attempt to pass unless you can:
options: a:Clearly see the road ahead and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:Pass as quickly as possible regardless of visibility.,c:Honk continuously while passing.,d:Cross double solid lines to pass.
note: Do not pass unless you can see ahead clearly, return safely before oncoming traffic, and it is legal to do so.

question: Who should wear seat belts for maximum effectiveness?
options: a:All occupants of the vehicle,b:The person driving the car only,c:Passengers only on long trips
note: Seat belts protect everyone; all occupants should wear lap and shoulder belts (or appropriate child restraints) on every trip.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a dashed white line on the highway?
options: a:When it is safe to change lanes.,b:Only during daytime hours.,c:Only when passing is illegal.,d:Never.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes when safe.

question: Why must you be careful when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.,b:Bicycles always have the right-of-way.,c:You will always be fined for passing too closely.,d:Bicyclists should ride on sidewalks only.
note: Passing motorists must be cautious because oncoming traffic may not expect you to leave your lane to pass a bicyclist.

question: What do work zone signs generally indicate?
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions and that extra caution is needed.,b:That construction will only occur during the day.,c:That you must immediately stop and back up.,d:That summer maintenance is underway.
note: Orange work zone signs warn drivers of changes, hazards, or workers on or near the roadway.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:You may change lanes or pass if it is safe,b:Lanes travel in opposite directions,c:Passing is never allowed,d:You must stop before crossing it
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is a correct rule to follow when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass,b:Pass on the right whenever possible,c:Try to get to the front of slow traffic by aggressive passing
note: When passing, signal well in advance (at least 100 feet), check mirrors and blind spots, and return when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for the other driver to pass,b:Speed up to prevent them,c:Maintain speed and ignore them,d:Brake suddenly to block them
note: Reduce speed slightly to create space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Yield to other cars,b:Slow down and prepare to stop,c:Go through the intersection quickly
note: A steady yellow light warns that a red light is about to appear; you should slow and prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely.

question: Which is important to do while driving on major highways?
options: a:Stay alert.,b:Keep your eyes fixed on a single point.,c:Turn off your headlights to save power.
note: On highways you should stay alert, keep your eyes moving, and be ready to react to hazards to avoid highway hypnosis.

question: When visibility is reduced by fog, what should you do?
options: a:Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.,b:Use high beams to see farther ahead.,c:Increase speed to quickly clear the fog.
note: In fog you should drive cautiously, reduce speed, avoid using high beams, and use low beams or fog lights if available.

question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane typically mark what?
options: a:Boundaries of a crosswalk; pedestrians in crosswalks must be given the right-of-way.,b:That vehicles have right-of-way over pedestrians.,c:That no one has right-of-way in the area.,d:A bike lane only
note: Solid white crosswalk lines indicate pedestrian crossing areas; drivers must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: At a crossing marked only with a crossbuck, how should you proceed?
options: a:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when no train is coming.,b:Assume the crossing is clear and proceed without looking.,c:Only proceed when a flagger signals you to go.,d:Speed up across the tracks to minimize time on them.
note: Cross only after ensuring no train is approaching from either direction; obey flaggers if present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who goes first?
options: a:The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.,b:The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.,c:One driver should continue driving without stopping.
note: At a four-way stop, the vehicle that arrives first proceeds first; if two arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: After being pulled over, should a driver immediately get out and approach the officer’s squad car?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Remain in your vehicle with your hands visible; do not exit unless the officer requests you to do so for safety reasons.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow changes to a steady green circular light, what must drivers do when turning?
options: a:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn under any circumstances.,c:You have absolute right-of-way to turn.,d:Stop and wait for a green arrow to reappear.
note: A green circular light allows the turn but drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: How can you avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spot?
options: a:Quickly glance over your shoulder before changing lanes,b:Adjust rearview mirrors every few minutes,c:Honk before changing lanes,d:Rely solely on side mirrors
note: Turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes; do not rely only on mirrors.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no signals or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Be prepared to yield to any train and cross only when safe.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Accelerate to cross quickly.,d:Assume the tracks are inactive.
note: Approach with caution and ensure there is room on the far side before crossing; never try to outdrive a train.

question: Turning your head to check blind spots before changing lanes is:
options: a:A good driving habit that should be practiced.,b:Unnecessary if you have mirrors.,c:A poor habit because it wastes time.,d:Required only for new drivers.
note: Checking blind spots by glancing over your shoulder is essential before lane changes or merging.

question: When making a left turn at an intersection, must you yield to oncoming bicyclists?
options: a:Yes—TRUE,b:No—FALSE,c:Only if the bicyclist is in a marked bike lane,d:Only at night
note: A left-turning motorist must yield to oncoming bicycles just as they would to oncoming motor vehicles.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them sharply away from the curb.,b:Turn them sharply toward the curb.,c:Point them straight ahead.
note: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn your wheels sharply away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: Which statements are true about seat belts and child restraints?
